actions.title: Deployments
actions.meaning: Every deployment in the namespace, with replicas, images and rollout state.

actions.title: Rollout status
actions.meaning: Whether the newest version of this deployment is fully rolled out.

actions.title: History
actions.meaning: The revisions this deployment has run, newest first, with their images.

actions.title: Roll back
actions.meaning: Run an earlier revision's pod template again. Pods are replaced one at a time.

actions.title: Pause rollout
actions.meaning: Stop this deployment reacting to template changes until it is resumed.

actions.title: Resume rollout
actions.meaning: Let a paused deployment roll out its template again.

actions.title: Set image
actions.meaning: Run a different image in one container. Only thales/ images are accepted.

actions.title: Restart rollout
actions.meaning: Replace every pod of this deployment, one at a time. Configuration is unchanged.

actions.title: Scale
actions.meaning: Set how many pods run, from 0 to 3. Scaling to 0 stops the workload.

actions.title: Events
actions.meaning: What the cluster recently said about this deployment and its pods.

actions.title: Logs
actions.meaning: The last lines a pod wrote, or follow them live for up to two minutes.

actions.title: Pods
actions.meaning: Pods in the namespace, or of one deployment, with status and restarts.

actions.title: Delete pod
actions.meaning: Delete one pod so its deployment or job replaces it. Only managed pods.

actions.title: Delete completed pods
actions.meaning: Remove pods that finished successfully. Running pods are never touched.

actions.title: Jobs
actions.meaning: Jobs in the namespace, newest first, and whether they succeeded.

actions.title: Job logs
actions.meaning: What a job's pod wrote.

actions.title: Delete job
actions.meaning: Delete a job and, in the background, its pods and their logs.

actions.title: Run template
actions.meaning: Start a job from a template shipped with Bothy, on the backend's current image.

actions.title: ConfigMap
actions.meaning: Every key and value of the thales ConfigMap, and which keys may be changed here.

actions.title: Change a key
actions.meaning: Set one allowlisted key. Pods read it at start, so it applies on their next restart.

actions.title: Change a key and restart
actions.meaning: Set one allowlisted key, then restart every deployment that reads this ConfigMap.

actions.title: Services
actions.meaning: Services, their ports and the pods they select.

actions.title: Routes
actions.meaning: OpenShift Routes: the hostnames that reach a service.

actions.title: Ingresses
actions.meaning: Ingress rules: hostnames and paths that reach a service.

actions.title: Volume claims
actions.meaning: Persistent volume claims, their size and whether they are bound.

actions.title: Network policies
actions.meaning: Which pods may talk to which, as the namespace's policies declare.

actions.title: Resource quotas
actions.meaning: The namespace's resource ceilings and how much is used.

actions.title: Limit ranges
actions.meaning: Default and maximum resources a container gets in this namespace.

actions.title: Namespace events
actions.meaning: Everything the cluster recently said about this namespace, newest first.

LOG_LEVEL.meaning: How much the backend and algorithm log.

DB_POOL_MAX.meaning: Database connections each backend replica may hold (1 to 20).

JOB_MAX_WORKERS.meaning: Solver jobs the algorithm runs at once (1 to 4).

CPSAT_TIME_LIMIT.meaning: Seconds CP-SAT may search, phase 1 and 2 together (1 to 570; live 540). It must finish 30 s before SYNC_OPTIMIZE_TIMEOUT_MS or the caller gets a 504 while the solve runs on.

CPSAT_PHASE2_TIME_LIMIT.meaning: Seconds reserved out of CPSAT_TIME_LIMIT for the phase-2 merge (0 to 285; live 120). Above half of CPSAT_TIME_LIMIT it is silently clamped; 0 reserves nothing.

CPSAT_SEARCH_WORKERS.meaning: CP-SAT search threads per solve (1 to 8; live 8). Times JOB_MAX_WORKERS against the pod's 2 CPUs, so 8 is already oversubscribed - this is the dial for turning it down.

CPSAT_RANDOM_SEED.meaning: The fixed seed that makes two solves of one input agree (0 to 999999999; live 42). OR-Tools takes a 32-bit seed, and a larger number fails at solve time, not at start.

CPSAT_RELATIVE_GAP_LIMIT.meaning: How far from proven-optimal CP-SAT may stop, as a fraction (0 to 0.999999; live 0.001). 0 means prove it exactly; 1 would accept the first answer found, so it is refused.

CPSAT_LEX_MERGE.meaning: Whether CP-SAT runs its phase-2 lexicographic merge (1 on, 0 off). Any other word, 2 included, stops the algorithm pod starting.

MILP_TIME_LIMIT.meaning: Seconds the MILP solver may run (1 to 570; live 540). Bounded by SYNC_OPTIMIZE_TIMEOUT_MS the same way CPSAT_TIME_LIMIT is.

MILP_GAP_ABS.meaning: How far from optimal the MILP solver may stop, in objective units - absolute, not a fraction (0 to 9.999; live 0.5). Above about 1 it can trade away a real decision.

DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS.meaning: Milliseconds to wait for a database connection before failing (1000 to 60000; live 10000). 0 would mean wait forever, so it is refused.

DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS.meaning: Milliseconds any one SQL statement may run, set on the server through the connection (1000 to 600000; live 60000). Migrations are bounded by it too.

DB_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S.meaning: Seconds the backend's entrypoint waits for the database before exiting non-zero (1 to 600; live 60). A leading zero would be read as octal by the shell that uses it.

JOB_CONTROL_TIMEOUT_MS.meaning: Milliseconds the backend waits on a job start, poll or cancel before answering 504 (1000 to 600000; live 30000). It must stay under GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_S.

JOB_TTL_SECONDS.meaning: Seconds a finished solver job stays readable before the algorithm forgets it (1 to 86400; live 900). Its result is held in memory until then.

SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS.meaning: Milliseconds the backend has to drain, flush and close on shutdown (1000 to 30000; live 10000). Above 30000 the pod is killed mid-sequence; 0 is legal to the code and refused here, because it abandons every step.

SYNC_OPTIMIZE_TIMEOUT_MS.meaning: Milliseconds the backend waits for a synchronous solve before answering 504 (600000 to 660000; live 600000). It has to sit above every solver limit plus 30 s and at or below GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_S, which leaves this window.

MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS.meaning: Milliseconds a migration waits for the migration lock before giving up and applying nothing (1000 to 600000; live 120000). DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS caps it in practice.

MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES.meaning: Largest request body the backend accepts, in bytes (10000000 to 69999999; live 10485760). It refuses to start below 7056044, the base64 cost of one 5 MiB attachment.

SSO_IDP_REFRESH_MS.meaning: Milliseconds between re-reads of the identity provider's descriptor (30000 to 9999999; live 60000). The live parser accepts any positive number, so this bound is the only thing between a typo and a poll loop against AD-FS.

ENABLED_ALGORITHMS.meaning: Which solvers the scheduler offers, in order (heuristic, milp, cpsat; live heuristic,milp,cpsat). The FIRST one is the default for any request that does not name a solver, so reordering changes the default. An unknown or repeated name, or an empty list, stops the backend starting.

configmapReasons.name: mirrored
configmapReasons.label: Mirrored elsewhere
configmapReasons.meaning: One stated number for the Route, the frontend's nginx and the registry they are both checked against. Changing it here alone desyncs three places.

configmapReasons.name: paired
configmapReasons.label: Only legal with another key
configmapReasons.meaning: Its legal values depend on another key's value, and this interface changes one key at a time.

configmapReasons.name: address
configmapReasons.label: An address
configmapReasons.meaning: Where something else is. It follows the deployment, so it is stated in the manifests with the rest of the topology.

configmapReasons.name: identity
configmapReasons.label: An identity setting
configmapReasons.meaning: It decides who the system thinks you are, or which tenant you are in. Changing it from a browser is the loop this interface must not close.

configmapReasons.name: security
configmapReasons.label: A security switch
configmapReasons.meaning: It decides who gets in, or how hard it is. It belongs to review, not to a table cell.

configmapReasons.name: manifests
configmapReasons.label: Set in the manifests
configmapReasons.meaning: It states which build this is, or something the release decides. It changes with a deployment, not at runtime.
